name: Working out whether a change in the code actually fixed a finding
description:
When a partner pushes a fix, something has to decide whether what they changed actually addresses what we told them. Today nothing does — a re-run simply reviews the new commit from scratch and forgets the previous one.

This is the piece that decides, and it rests on one hard rule: **a finding counts as fixed only when the code at its place actually changed.** Never because we simply did not find it again the second time. Not finding something again is the weakest evidence there is — the second review may have been thinner, the engine may have drifted or failed outright — and treating it as proof is exactly how a real problem quietly disappears.

So it works in two steps:

- **Was the place touched at all?** Compare the two commits. If the code the finding points at was not changed, the finding stays open — full stop, no second opinion needed.
- **Does the change address it?** Where it was touched, read the surrounding code and decide. A fix made fifty lines away — a check moved, validation pulled into a helper — has to be recognised, or we end up telling a partner that something they did fix is still open.

Everything uncertain lands on "still open": a commit we can no longer reach after a rewritten history, an answer we cannot read, a budget we ran out of. That direction is deliberate and one-sided. Over-reporting costs the partner one extra look; under-reporting loses a real finding.

**Done when:** for a finding still open from an earlier round, the tool decides new / still open / fixed, records what that decision was based on, and every way the decision can be uncertain has its own test proving it lands on "still open".

Plan: https://github.com/shoptet/aidev-apps/pull/27 — batch 2, tasks T5 and T6.
